_comment: The trade economy (scripts/economy/economy_model.gd). Every port, every day: stock += production x season + imports - consumption - exports - spoilage. Price = base x (normal / stock) ^ elasticity, clamped. Consumption falls when a good is dear (demand_response); outside merchants bring more when it's dear and carry more off when it's cheap (supply_response), so each port settles at a price of its own, and the player's trades knock it off balance for a while. Quantities are units of the good per day. Numbers are design choices, roughly right for 1650-1730, not history.
_goods: Goods (data/goods.json): Trade goods. base_price: the Caribbean average (prices swing around it). weight: tons of hold per unit (bulk). spoils: fraction of a port's stock lost per day. demand: necessity (price jumps when short; people buy it anyway) or luxury (price reacts gently; people go without) or treasure (barely moves). origin: european (shipped from Europe), colonial (grown here), supply, treasure; it sets how outside merchants carry it (data/economy.json). season: production curve in economy.json. economy false: outside the market (water is free for the taking).
_cover_days: Normal stock is this many days of what a port makes plus what it uses. Smaller means the player's trades move prices more (chosen for fun: 20 days, not a realistic season's stock).
_duty: Taken on every legal purchase and sale, on top of a port's tariff (set by its politics). Smuggled goods pay none.

per_1000._comment: What 1,000 townsfolk use in a day, before their port's tags.

tag_use._comment: Multipliers on consumption by a port's tags: plantations eat and break tools, garrisons burn powder.

outside._comment: Stand-in for merchant traffic until it's simulated ship by ship (market milestone 2): the off-map trade with Europe and other colonies. import: share of a port's use that outside merchants bring at normal prices; export: share of its production they carry off; reexport: share of its use they carry off again (a port that makes none still sells some on).
outside._faction_import: Spain forbids trade with foreigners: European goods reach its ports only by the fleets and smugglers, so they're scarce and dear. Its own coasting trade from the mainland (not on the map) brings colonial goods and food instead. England's colonies get London's goods directly and plentifully.

traffic._comment: Merchant voyages between the ports (scripts/economy/traffic.gd). Since market milestone 2 the outside trade above is only the trade with Europe and North America; goods move around the Caribbean in these ships.
traffic._tramp_chance: After unloading, a ship looks for a cargo where she is (so small ports get ships too) or goes home.
traffic._min_margin: A merchant sails only for a known price gap of at least this much (after the spreads), and stops buying when the next unit isn't worth it.
traffic._approach_share: A ship taken near a port frightens every route into it: this share of the loss's risk goes to the port's approaches.
traffic._risk_breeds_pirates: Where ships have been taken lately, more get taken: pirates go where the hunting is good.
traffic._smugglers: Merchants who run forbidden goods into Spanish ports. Each voyage risks seizure by the guarda costas.

fleets._comment: The convoys (scripts/economy/fleets.gd). month: when they're due; delay_days: how late; brings: days of each port's use, landed on arrival; fair_days: how long they stay; fair_use: use multipliers while they're in (crowds at a fair, a convoy buying cargo for home); takes: the share of each port's stock they carry off when they sail. irregular_from / skip_chance: after 1700 the Spanish fleets often didn't sail at all.

information._comment: What the player knows (scripts/ports.gd). Prices you saw yourself, heard on the quay (each port's news is only as fresh as the last ship in from where it's about), found in a captured ship's papers, or picked up as tavern rumour (sometimes false). Your best trader (captain or officer) estimates today's price from old news: the older the news, the more it leans on what the port usually fetches, and the error shrinks with trade skill and allies.

shocks._comment: Random shocks (scripts/economy/shocks.gd): about one a month somewhere. months: when it can happen; tags: the ports it can hit (any of these tags); weight: how often, against the others; effects: the shared vocabulary (EconomyModel.apply_effect: port_damage, flows, stock, spread, sailings, route_risk, market_shock); goods: ids, made, used, all, random (one this port makes) or random_used (one it ships in). The news goes out at sailing speed.

hurricane.name: Hurricane
hurricane.news: A hurricane has torn through {port}: roofs gone, warehouses flooded, the fields flattened.

epidemic.name: Fever
epidemic.news: Yellow fever in {port}. Half the town is sick, and few ships will put in.

bad_harvest.name: Poor harvest
bad_harvest.news: The {good} crop has failed around {port}. Prices there are climbing.

glut.name: Bumper harvest
glut.news: Warehouses in {port} are overflowing with {good}. It's going for nothing.

shortage.name: Shortage
shortage.news: {good} is fetching a fortune in {port}. They can't get enough of it.

bankruptcy.name: A merchant house fails
bankruptcy.news: A great merchant house in {port} has failed. Credit is gone, and few ships are fitting out there.

sacked.name: Sacked
sacked.news: {port} has been sacked: the warehouses emptied, the churches stripped, half the town burned.

warehouse_fire.name: Warehouse fire
warehouse_fire.news: Fire on the waterfront at {port}: a row of warehouses has burned to the ground.

garrison_reinforced.name: Garrison reinforced
garrison_reinforced.news: Fresh troops have landed at {port}. They'll need feeding, and powder.

coin_shortage.name: No coin
coin_shortage.news: There's no coin to be had in {port}. Merchants trade in sugar and promises, and drive hard bargains.

piracy_wave.name: Pirates about
piracy_wave.news: Pirates are working the approaches to {port}. Ships are being taken in sight of the fort.

_sailing: Outside trade by month: fewer ships sail in the hurricane season (June to November).

seasons._comment: Production by month, January first. Each curve is scaled to average 1.

molasses.low: Little coming from the boiling houses

tobacco.low: Last year's leaf is running out

indigo.low: Few indigo cakes this time of year
